faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium intramedullary nail?
faq.a: Grade 23 ELI (ASTM F136) is the standard for surgical implants. Extra-low interstitials (O<=0.13%) improve fracture toughness. Do not substitute industrial TC4.

faq.q: How is a titanium intramedullary nail manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium intramedullary nail is manufactured using VAR melting; Closed-die hot forging; CNC swiss turning; Thread rolling. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Ti-6Al-4V ELI (ASTM F136) for titanium intramedullary nail?
faq.a: Other materials such as steel or aluminum are significantly heavier and lack the corrosion resistance required for long-term service.

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium intramedullary nail?
faq.a: Titanium Intramedullary Nail components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.

faq.q: What are common failure modes for titanium intramedullary nail?
faq.a: Common failure modes include Self-tapping threads require no burrs; use thread rolling instead of cutting; Implant surface must be free of iron contamination; use dedicated Ti-alloy tooling. Proper material selection, manufacturing process control, and inspection mitigate these risks.

faq.q: What surface treatments are available for titanium intramedullary nail?
faq.a: Common surface treatments include Passivation ASTM F86. These enhance corrosion resistance, wear properties, and aesthetic appearance.
